newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania coalminers end strike, win pay concessions.
newsitem.headline: Romania coalminers end strike, win pay concessions.

text.p: Thousands of miners from Romania's western Jiu Valley coalfield ended a 10-day strike on Friday, after winning pay concessions from the new centrist government.
The strike launched by the Jiu Valley miners, Romania's most militant, had posed the biggest challenge to the ruling centrists since they ousted ex-communists in last year's polls.

"We won, and we managed to do it without violence," miners' leader Romeo Beja told some 5,000 cheering miners gathered outside the headquarters of the mine authority in Petrosani, 400 km (250 miles) west of Bucharest.

Beja announced the pay concessions after talks with government officials earlier on Friday. He said miners would get a 23 pay increase next month, and a further seven percent in August. "This 30 percent rise represents our victory. Actually, we got what we were entitled to, we never begged for our rights."

The deal was struck after President Emil Constantinescu, who defeated an ex-communist in last November's elections, summoned ministers to his Cotroceni palace late on Thursday to find a solution to the miners' protests.

On Friday Constantinescu met leaders of Romania's biggest labour unions, to find common ground on tough reforms pledged by the government, including restructuring of loss-making communist-era industries.
Government negotiators said the deal would not punch a hole in the country's austerity budget. The money would be released by the Regie Autonone of Coal (RAH), local mining authority.
"The pay rises beyond our initial offer of 15 percent will come from the RAH budget," said deputy finance minister Dan Rusanu, one of the negotiators sent to the area on Friday.

"The funds will come from restructuring the RAH," he said in a reference to the government's plans to turn the "regies autonomes" in industries like mining, where state has a monopoly, into commercial companies up for privatisation.
The government had said the miners' 15 percent pay rise would result from tax cuts due to come into effect in August.

Miners earn nearly twice the average Romanian wage, which is equivalent to $80 a month, and still have communist-era benefits like bonuses, cheap electricity and rent. But many say they live and work in intolerable conditions.

The Jiu Valley miners had also demanded the release of their union boss, Miron Cosma, who is on trial over his role in leading miners' riots which toppled Romania's first post-communist government in 1991. Beja said they would pursue the case through legal channels.
The miners dispersed quietly from Petrosani's drab square where they had protested over the past 10 days. Their leaders said work in the pits would resume later on Friday.
Constantinescu has urged top economic ministers to produce a plan to restructure Romania's loss-making coal sector and develop the Jiu Valley.

His centrists blame ex-president Ion Iliescu for miner-led violence in the early post-communist years, in which seven people were killed. Iliescu seeks re-election this wekend as head of his Party of Social Democracy, which is split by a rist with moderates after their election rout last November.
